claims.text: Ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering refines the alloy microstructure.
The as-processed alloy is a non-equilibrium, metastable, solid-solution-containing Mg high-entropy alloy.
The initial ball-milled and SPS-processed state contains little or no intermetallic precipitation.
Controlled thermal exposure causes Mg-rich intermetallic compounds to precipitate from the metastable matrix.
The precipitation of Mg-rich intermetallic phases proceeds by thermally activated, diffusion-controlled nucleation and growth.
The refined grain-boundary network promotes nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Thermal aging increases the concentration of Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Coherent, finely dispersed Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates pin defect sites.
Coherent, finely dispersed Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates stabilize a protective oxide scale.
Stabilization of the protective oxide scale by appropriately dispersed precipitates preserves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Appropriately coherent and dispersed intermetallic precipitates hinder corrosive attack.
Excessive, incoherent, or heterogeneous intermetallic growth compromises surface passivation and protective-scale integrity.
Excessive or incoherent intermetallic growth degrades corrosion and oxidation performance.
A moderate, well-dispersed intermetallic phase after aging should correlate with maintained or slightly enhanced corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
A moderate, well-dispersed intermetallic phase after aging should correlate with maintained or slightly enhanced oxidation resistance relative to the initial state.
Negligible intermetallic formation after aging will be associated with degraded performance.
Overly extensive intermetallic formation after aging will be associated with degraded performance.
The proposed transformation is expected under sustained thermal exposure above approximately 350 degrees Celsius.
Conditions outside the stated service regime should produce markedly different transformation pathways.
